agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## 1. What does this tool do? *grex* is a library as well as a command-line utility that is meant to simplify the often complicated and tedious task of creating regular expressions. It does so by automatically generating a single regular expression from user-provided test cases. The resulting expression is guaranteed to match the test cases which it was generated from. This project has started as a Rust port of the JavaScript tool [*regexgen*](https://github.com/devongovett/regexgen) written by [Devon Govett](https://github.com/devongovett). Although a lot of further useful features could be added to it, its development was apparently ceased several years ago. The plan is now to add these new features to *grex* as Rust really shines when it comes to command-line tools. *grex* offers all features that *regexgen* provides, and more. The philosophy of this project is to generate the most specific regular expression possible by default which exactly matches the given input only and nothing else. With the use of command-line flags (in the CLI tool) or preprocessing methods (in the library), more generalized expressions can be created. The produced expressions are [Perl-compatible regular expressions](https://www.pcre.org) which are also compatible with the regular expression parser in Rust's [*regex* crate](https://crates.io/crates/regex). Other regular expression parsers or respective libraries from other programming languages have not been tested so far, but they ought to be mostly compatible as well. ## 2. Do I still need to learn to write regexes then? **Definitely, yes!** Using the standard settings, *grex* produces a regular expression that is guaranteed to match only the test cases given as input and nothing else. This has been verified by [property tests](https://github.com/pemistahl/grex/blob/main/tests/property_tests.rs). However, if the conversion to shorthand character classes such as `\w` is enabled, the resulting regex matches a much wider scope of test cases. Knowledge about the consequences of this conversion is essential for finding a correct regular expression f 8576 characters elided sions, the conversion to surrogate pairs is necessary. More information on that matter can be found [here](https://mathiasbynens.be/notes/javascript-unicode). ```rust use grex::RegExpBuilder; let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["You smell like 💩."]) .with_escaped_non_ascii_chars(true) .build(); assert_eq!(regexp, "^You smell like \\u{d83d}\\u{dca9}\\.$"); ``` #### 5.2.5 Case-insensitive matching The regular expressions that *grex* generates are case-sensitive by default. Case-insensitive matching can be enabled like so: ```rust use grex::RegExpBuilder; let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["big", "BIGGER"]) .with_case_insensitive_matching() .build(); assert_eq!(regexp, "(?i)^big(?:ger)?$"); ``` #### 5.2.6 Capturing Groups Non-capturing groups are used by default. Extending the previous example, you can switch to capturing groups instead. ```rust use grex::RegExpBuilder; let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["big", "BIGGER"]) .with_case_insensitive_matching() .with_capturing_groups() .build(); assert_eq!(regexp, "(?i)^big(ger)?$"); ``` #### 5.2.7 Verbose mode If you find the generated regular expression hard to read, you can enable verbose mode. The expression is then put on multiple lines and indented to make it more pleasant to the eyes. ```rust use grex::RegExpBuilder; use indoc::indoc; let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "b", "bcd"]) .with_verbose_mode() .build(); assert_eq!(regexp, indoc!( r#" (?x) ^ (?: b (?: cd )? | a ) $"# )); ``` #### 5.2.8 Disable anchors By default, the anchors `^` and `$` are put around every generated regular expression in order to ensure that it matches only the test cases given as input. Often enough, however, it is desired to use the generated pattern as part of a larger one. For this purpose, the anchors can be disabled, either separately or both of them. ```rust use grex::RegExpBuilder; let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "aa", "aaa"]) .without_anchors() .build(); assert_eq!(regexp, "a(?:aa?)?"); ``` ### 5.3 Examples The following examples show the various supported regex syntax features: ```shell $ grex a b c ^[a-c]$ $ grex a c d e f ^[ac-f]$ $ grex a b x de ^(?:de|[abx])$ $ grex abc bc ^a?bc$ $ grex a b bc ^(?:bc?|a)$ $ grex [a-z] ^\[a\-z\]$ $ grex -r b ba baa baaa ^b(?:a{1,3})?$ $ grex -r b ba baa baaaa ^b(?:a{1,2}|a{4})?$ $ grex y̆ a z ^(?:y̆|[az])$ Note: Grapheme y̆ consists of two Unicode symbols: U+0079 (Latin Small Letter Y) U+0306 (Combining Breve) $ grex "I ♥ cake" "I ♥ cookies" ^I ♥ c(?:ookies|ake)$ Note: Input containing blank space must be surrounded by quotation marks. ``` The string `"I ♥♥♥ 36 and ٣ and 💩💩."` serves as input for the following examples using the command-line notation: ```shell $ grex ^I ♥♥♥ 36 and ٣ and 💩💩\.$ $ grex -e ^I \u{2665}\u{2665}\u{2665} 36 and \u{663} and \u{1f4a9}\u{1f4a9}\.$ $ grex -e --with-surrogates ^I \u{2665}\u{2665}\u{2665} 36 and \u{663} and \u{d83d}\u{dca9}\u{d83d}\u{dca9}\.$ $ grex -d ^I ♥♥♥ \d\d and \d and 💩💩\.$ $ grex -s ^I\s♥♥♥\s36\sand\s٣\sand\s💩💩\.$ $ grex -w ^\w ♥♥♥ \w\w \w\w\w \w \w\w\w 💩💩\.$ $ grex -D ^\D\D\D\D\D\D36\D\D\D\D\D٣\D\D\D\D\D\D\D\D$ $ grex -S ^\S \S\S\S \S\S \S\S\S \S \S\S\S \S\S\S$ $ grex -dsw ^\w\s♥♥♥\s\d\d\s\w\w\w\s\d\s\w\w\w\s💩💩\.$ $ grex -dswW ^\w\s\W\W\W\s\d\d\s\w\w\w\s\d\s\w\w\w\s\W\W\W$ $ grex -r ^I ♥{3} 36 and ٣ and 💩{2}\.$ $ grex -er ^I \u{2665}{3} 36 and \u{663} and \u{1f4a9}{2}\.$ $ grex -er --with-surrogates ^I \u{2665}{3} 36 and \u{663} and (?:\u{d83d}\u{dca9}){2}\.$ $ grex -dgr ^I ♥{3} \d(\d and ){2}💩{2}\.$ $ grex -rs ^I\s♥{3}\s36\sand\s٣\sand\s💩{2}\.$ $ grex -rw ^\w ♥{3} \w(?:\w \w{3} ){2}💩{2}\.$ $ grex -Dr ^\D{6}36\D{5}٣\D{8}$ $ grex -rS ^\S \S(?:\S{2} ){2}\S{3} \S \S{3} \S{3}$ $ grex -rW ^I\W{5}36\Wand\W٣\Wand\W{4}$ $ grex -drsw ^\w\s♥{3}\s\d(?:\d\s\w{3}\s){2}💩{2}\.$ $ grex -drswW ^\w\s\W{3}\s\d(?:\d\s\w{3}\s){2}\W{3}$ ``` ## 6. ### 5.2 The library

#### 5.2.1 Default settings

Test cases are passed either from a collection via [`RegExpBuilder::from()`](https://docs.rs/grex/1.4.6/grex/struct.RegExpBuilder.html#method.from) 
or from a file via [`RegExpBuilder::from_file()`](https://docs.rs/grex/1.4.6/grex/struct.RegExpBuilder.html#method.from_file).
If read from a file, each test case must be on a separate line. Lines may be ended with either a newline `\n` or a carriage
return with a line feed `\r\n`.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "aa", "aaa"]).build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^a(?:aa?)?$");
```

#### 5.2.2 Convert to character classes

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "aa", "123"])
    .with_conversion_of_digits()
    .with_conversion_of_words()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^(\\d\\d\\d|\\w(?:\\w)?)$");
```

#### 5.2.3 Convert repeated substrings

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["aa", "bcbc", "defdefdef"])
    .with_conversion_of_repetitions()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^(?:a{2}|(?:bc){2}|(?:def){3})$");
```

By default, *grex* converts each substring this way which is at least a single character long 
and which is subsequently repeated at least once. You can customize these two parameters if you like.

In the following example, the test case `aa` is not converted to `a{2}` because the repeated substring 
`a` has a length of 1, but the minimum substring length has been set to 2.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["aa", "bcbc", "defdefdef"])
    .with_conversion_of_repetitions()
    .with_minimum_substring_length(2)
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^(?:aa|(?:bc){2}|(?:def){3})$");
```

Setting a minimum number of 2 repetitions in the next example, only the test case `defdefdef` will be
converted because it is the only one that is repeated twice.

```rust
let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["aa", "bcbc", "defdefdef"])
    .with_conversion_of_repetitions()
    .with_minimum_repetitions(2)
```

#### 5.2.4 Escape non-ascii characters

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["You smell like 💩."])
    .with_escaping_of_non_ascii_chars(false)
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^You smell like \\u{1f4a9}\\.$");
```

Old versions of JavaScript do not support unicode escape sequences for the astral code planes 
(range `U+010000` to `U+10FFFF`). In order to support these symbols in JavaScript regular 
expressions, the conversion to surrogate pairs is necessary. More information on that matter 
can be found [here](https://mathiasbynens.be/notes/javascript-unicode).

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["You smell like 💩."])
    .with_escaped_non_ascii_chars(true)
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^You smell like \\u{d83d}\\u{dca9}\\.$");
```

#### 5.2.5 Case-insensitive matching

The regular expressions that *grex* generates are case-sensitive by default.
Case-insensitive matching can be enabled like so:

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["big", "BIGGER"])
    .with_case_insensitive_matching()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "(?i)^big(?:ger)?$");
```

#### 5.2.6 Capturing Groups

Non-capturing groups are used by default. 
Extending the previous example, you can switch to capturing groups instead.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["big", "BIGGER"])
    .with_case_insensitive_matching()
    .with_capturing_groups()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "(?i)^big(ger)?$");
```

#### 5.2.7 Verbose mode

If you find the generated regular expression hard to read, you can enable verbose mode.
The expression is then put on multiple lines and indented to make it more pleasant to the eyes.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;
use indoc::indoc;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "b", "bcd"])
    .with_verbose_mode()
    .build();

assert_eq!(regexp, indoc!(
    r#"
    (?x)
    ^
      (?:
        b
        (?:
          cd
        )?
        |
        a
      )
    $"#
));
```

#### 5.2.8 Disable anchors

By default, the anchors `^` and `$` are put around every generated regular expression in order
to ensure that it matches only the test cases given as input. Often enough, however, it is
desired to use the generated pattern as part of a larger one. For this purpose, the anchors
can be disabled, either separately or both of them.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "aa", "aaa"])
    .without_anchors()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "a(?:aa?)?");
```

### 5.3 Examples

The following examples show the various supported regex syntax features:

```shell
$ grex a b c
^[a-c]$

$ grex a c d e f
^[ac-f]$
```

## 6. How to build?

In order to build the source code yourself, you need the 
[stable Rust toolchain](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) installed on your machine 
so that [*cargo*](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/), the Rust package manager is available.
**Please note**: Rust >= 1.70.0 is required to build the CLI. For the library part, Rust < 1.70.0 is sufficient.

```shell
git clone https://github.com/pemistahl/grex.git
cd grex
cargo build
```

The source code is accompanied by an extensive test suite consisting of unit tests, integration 
tests and property tests. For running them, simply say:

```shell
cargo test
```

# Unicode helpers
def is_decimal(ch):
    # Nd category
    return unicodedata.category(ch) == 'Nd'

def is_space(ch):
    # use .isspace() which covers White_Space
    return ch.isspace()

def is_word(ch):
    cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
    if cat.startswith('L'):  # Letter
        return True
    if cat.startswith('M'):  # Mark
        return True
    if cat == 'Nd':
        return True
    if cat == 'Pc':
        return True
    if ch == '_':
        return True
    return False

    specials = set(r"\.^$|?*+()[]{}-")
    if ch == '\t':
        return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n':
        return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r':
        return r'\r'
    if ch == '\f':
        return r'\f'
    if ch == '\v':
        return r'\v'
    if ch in specials:

    # For other control chars?
    if ch == '-':

    return ch

    if ch == ']':

    if ch == '[':

    if ch == '\t':
        return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n':
        return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r':

def eprint(*a, **kw):
    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, **kw)

def is_decimal(ch):
    return unicodedata.category(ch) == 'Nd'

def is_space(ch):
    return ch.isspace()

def is_word(ch):
    cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
    if cat.startswith('L'): return True
    if cat.startswith('M'): return True
    if cat == 'Nd': return True
    if cat == 'Pc': return True
    if ch == '_': return True
    return False

def escape_literal(ch):
    if ch == '\t':
        return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n':
        return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r':
        return r'\r'
    # For other whitespace like \f etc maybe not needed
    specials = r"\.^$|?*+()[]{}"
    if ch in specials:
        return '\\' + ch
    if ch == '-':
        return r'\-'
    return ch

def escape_class_char(ch):
    if ch == '\\': return r'\\'
    if ch == ']': return r'\]'
    if ch == '[': return r'\['
    if ch == '^': return r'\^'
    if ch == '-': return r'\-'
    if ch == '\t': return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n': return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r': return r'\r'
    return ch

def convert_char(ch, flags):
    if flags.get('digits') and is_decimal(ch):
        return r'\d'
    if flags.get('spaces') and is_space(ch):
        return r'\s'
    if flags.get('words') and is_word(ch):
        return r'\w'
    if flags.get('non_digits') and not is_decimal(ch):
        return r'\D'
    if flags.get('non_words') and not is_word(ch):
        return r'\W'
    if flags.get('non_spaces') and not is_space(ch):
        return r'\S'
    return None

def unicode_escape(ch, with_surrogates):
    code = ord(ch)
    if with_surrogates and code >= 0x10000:
        high = 0xD800 + ((code - 0x10000) >> 10)
        low = 0xDC00 + ((code - 0x10000) & 0x3FF)
        return f"\\u{{{high:x}}}\\u{{{low:x}}}"
    else:
        return f"\\u{{{code:x}}}"

def transform_string(s, flags):
    # s is original case (already lowercased if ignore-case)
    tokens = []
    for ch in s:
        conv = convert_char(ch, flags)
        if conv is not None:
            tokens.append(conv)
            continue
        if flags.get('escape') and ord(ch) > 127:
            tokens.append(unicode_escape(ch, flags.get('with_surrogates', False)))
            continue
        tokens.append(escape_literal(ch))
    return tokens

# Trie
class Node:
    def __init__(self):
        self.children = {}
        self.terminal = False

def build_trie(token_lists):
    root = Node()
    for tokens in token_lists:
        node = root
        for tok in tokens:
            if tok not in node.children:
                node.children[tok] = Node()
            node = node.children[tok]
        node.terminal = True
    return root

def charset_for_tokens(sorted_tokens):
    # sorted_tokens are branch strings that are single char tokens (escaped)
    # Recover original chars for range detection
    # For sorting, we already sorted by original ord, just build
    original_chars = []
    for tok in sorted_tokens:
        if len(tok) == 1:
            original_chars.append(tok)
        elif len(tok) == 2 and tok[0] == '\\':
            esc = tok[1]
            if esc == 't':
                original_chars.append('\t')
            elif esc == 'n':
                original_chars.append('\n')
            elif esc == 'r':
                original_chars.append('\r')
            elif esc in '.^$|?*+()[]{}-\\':
                original_chars.append(esc)
            else:
                original_chars.append(esc)
        elif tok.startswith(r'\u{'):
            # Try parse hex
            try:
                start = tok.find('{')+1
                end = tok.find('}')
                hex_str = tok[start:end]
                code = int(hex_str, 16)
                original_chars.append(chr(code))
            except:
                original_chars.append(tok)
        else:
            original_chars.append(tok)
    # Now chars are already sorted by ord? Assume sorted_tokens sorted, but original order may differ for escaped?
    # Sort original_chars by ord
    # But need to keep sorted order of tokens correspond to sorted original? We'll re-sort original_chars
    # Actually we want charset content sorted by original char codepoint
    # So sort pairs
    # We'll sort original_chars
    chars = sorted(original_chars, key=lambda c: ord(c))
    # Build runs
    content_parts = []
    i=0
    n=len(chars)
    while i < n:
        start = chars[i]
        j=i
        while j+1 < n and ord(chars[j+1]) == ord(chars[j]) + 1:
            j+=1
        run_len = j - i + 1
        if run_len >= 3:
            content_parts.append(f"{escape_class_char(chars[i])}-{escape_class_char(chars[j])}")
        else:
            for k in range(i, j+1):
                content_parts.append(escape_class_char(chars[k]))
        i = j+1
    return f"[{''.join(content_parts)}]"

def lcp_of_list(strs):
    if not strs:
        return ""
    pref = strs[0]
    for s in strs[1:]:
        i=0
        lim = min(len(pref), len(s))
        while i < lim and pref[i]==s[i]:
            i+=1
        pref = pref[:i]
        if not pref:
            break
    return pref

def lcs_of_list(strs):
    if not strs:
        return ""
    rev = [s[::-1] for s in strs]
    rev_pref = lcp_of_list(rev)
    return rev_pref[::-1]

def is_single_char_branch(b):
    if b in (r'\d', r'\D', r'\s', r'\S', r'\w', r'\W'):
        return False
    if b.startswith('[') and b.endswith(']'):
        return False
    if b.startswith('('):
        return False
    if '{' in b:
        return False
    if b.startswith(r'\u{'):
        if b.count(r'\u{') == 1 and b.endswith('}'):
            return True
        return False
    if len(b)==1:
        return True
    if len(b)==2 and b[0]=='\\':
        return True
    return False

def branch_ord(b):
    if len(b)==1:
        return ord(b)
    if len(b)==2 and b[0]=='\\':
        esc = b[1]
        if esc=='t': return ord('\t')
        if esc=='n': return ord('\n')
        if esc=='r': return ord('\r')
        return ord(esc)
    if b.startswith(r'\u{'):
        try:
            start=b.find('{')+1
            end=b.find('}')
            return int(b[start:end],16)
        except:
            return ord(b[0])
    return ord(b[0])

def make_optional(branch_str, capture):
    if not branch_str:
        return ""
    if branch_str.startswith('[') and branch_str.endswith(']'):
        return branch_str + '?'
    if branch_str in (r'\d',r'\D',r'\s',r'\S',r'\w',r'\W',r'\t',r'\n',r'\r'):
        return branch_str + '?'
    if len(branch_str)==1:
        return branch_str + '?'
    if len(branch_str)==2 and branch_str[0]=='\\':
        return branch_str + '?'
    if branch_str.startswith(r'\u{') and branch_str.count(r'\u{')==1 and branch_str.endswith('}'):
        return branch_str + '?'
    prefix = '(' if capture else '(?:'
    return f"{prefix}{branch_str})?"

def branches_to_regex(branches, capture, flags):
    if not branches:
        return ""
    if len(branches)==1:
        return branches[0]
    # check if all singles -> charset
    if all(is_single_char_branch(b) for b in branches):
        # sort by ord
        sorted_br = sorted(branches, key=branch_ord)
        return charset_for_tokens(sorted_br)
    # try prefix factoring
    lcp = lcp_of_list(branches)
    if lcp:
        stripped = [b[len(lcp):] for b in branches]
        has_empty = "" in stripped
        non_empty = [s for s in stripped if s != ""]
        if not non_empty:
            return lcp
        if has_empty:
            suffix_re = branches_to_regex(non_empty, capture, flags)
            # make suffix optional
            suffix_opt = make_optional(suffix_re, capture)
            return lcp + suffix_opt
        else:
            suffix_re = branches_to_regex(non_empty, capture, flags)
            return lcp + suffix_re
    lcs = lcs_of_list(branches)
    if lcs:
        stripped = [b[:-len(lcs)] if lcs else b for b in branches]
        has_empty = "" in stripped
        non_empty = [s for s in stripped if s != ""]
        if not non_empty:
            return lcs
        if has_empty:
            prefix_re = branches_to_regex(non_empty, capture, flags)
            prefix_opt = make_optional(prefix_re, capture)
            return prefix_opt + lcs
        else:
            prefix_re = branches_to_regex(non_empty, capture, flags)
            return prefix_re + lcs
    # fallback alternation with merging singles
    singles = [b for b in branches if is_single_char_branch(b)]
    multis = [b for b in branches if not is_single_char_branch(b)]
    options = []
    if multis:
        multis_sorted = sorted(multis)  # lexicographic
        options.extend(multis_sorted)
    if singles:
        if len(singles) >= 2:
            sorted_singles = sorted(singles, key=branch_ord)
            charset = charset_for_tokens(sorted_singles)
            options.append(charset)
        else:
            options.extend(singles)
    if len(options)==1:
        return options[0]
    # Sort options: multis first as above, but singles charset at end
    prefix = '(' if capture else '(?:'
    inner = '|'.join(options)
    return f"{prefix}{inner})"

def trie_to_regex(node, capture, flags):
    branches = []
    for ch in sorted(node.children.keys()):
        child = node.children[ch]
        child_re = trie_to_regex(child, capture, flags)
        branch = ch + child_re
        branches.append(branch)
    has_empty = node.terminal
    if not branches:
        return ""
    if has_empty:
        if len(branches)==1:
            return make_optional(branches[0], capture)
        else:
            alt = branches_to_regex(branches, capture, flags)
            return make_optional(alt, capture)
    else:
        if len(branches)==1:
            return branches[0]
        else:
            return branches_to_regex(branches, capture, flags)

    cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
    if cat.startswith('L'): return True
    if cat.startswith('M'): return True
    if cat == 'Nd': return True
    if cat == 'Pc': return True
    if ch == '_': return True
    return False

def escape_literal(ch):
    if ch == '\t': return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n': return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r': return r'\r'
    specials = set(r"\.^$|?*+()[]{}")
    if ch in specials:
        return '\\' + ch
    if ch == '-':
        return r'\-'
    return ch

def escape_class_char(ch):
    if ch == '\\': return r'\\'
    if ch == ']': return r'\]'
    if ch == '[': return r'\['
    if ch == '^': return r'\^'
    if ch == '-': return r'\-'
    if ch == '\t': return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n': return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r': return r'\r'
    return ch

def convert_char(ch, flags):
    if flags.get('digits') and is_decimal(ch):
        return r'\d'
    if flags.get('spaces') and is_space(ch):
        return r'\s'
    if flags.get('words') and is_word(ch):
        return r'\w'
    if flags.get('non_digits') and not is_decimal(ch):
        return r'\D'
    if flags.get('non_words') and not is_word(ch):
        return r'\W'
    if flags.get('non_spaces') and not is_space(ch):
        return r'\S'
    return None

def unicode_escape(ch, with_surrogates):
    code = ord(ch)
    if with_surrogates and code >= 0x10000:
        high = 0xD800 + ((code - 0x10000) >> 10)
        low = 0xDC00 + ((code - 0x10000) & 0x3FF)
        return f"\\u{{{high:x}}}\\u{{{low:x}}}"
    else:
        return f"\\u{{{code:x}}}"

def transform_string(s, flags):
    tokens=[]
    for ch in s:
        conv=convert_char(ch, flags)
        if conv is not None:
            tokens.append(conv)
            continue
        if flags.get('escape') and ord(ch) > 127:
            tokens.append(unicode_escape(ch, flags.get('with_surrogates', False)))
            continue
        tokens.append(escape_literal(ch))
    return tokens

            node=node.children[tok]
        node.terminal=True
    return root

        if len(tok)==1:
            orig.append(tok)
        elif len(tok)==2 and tok[0]=='\\':
            esc=tok[1]
            if esc=='t': orig.append('\t')
            elif esc=='n': orig.append('\n')
            elif esc=='r': orig.append('\r')
            elif esc in '.^$|?*+()[]{}-\\': orig.append(esc)
            else: orig.append(esc)
        elif tok.startswith(r'\u{'):
            try:
                s=tok.find('{')+1
                e=tok.find('}')
                orig.append(chr(int(tok[s:e],16)))
            except:
                orig.append(tok)
        else:
            orig.append(tok)
    chars=sorted(orig, key=lambda c: ord(c))
    parts=[]
    i=0
    n=len(chars)
    while i < n:
        j=i
        while j+1<n and ord(chars[j+1])==ord(chars[j])+1:
            j+=1
        run=j-i+1
        if run>=3:
            parts.append(f"{escape_class_char(chars[i])}-{escape_class_char(chars[j])}")

    return f"[{''.join(parts)}]"

def lcp(lst):
    if not lst: return ""
    pref=lst[0]
    for s in lst[1:]:
        i=0
        lim=min(len(pref), len(s))
        while i<lim and pref[i]==s[i]:
            i+=1
        pref=pref[:i]
        if not pref: break
    return pref

    if not lst: return ""
    rev=[s[::-1] for s in lst]
    rp=lcp(rev)
    return rp[::-1]

    if '{' in tok: return False
    if tok.startswith(r'\u{'):
        return tok.count(r'\u{')==1 and tok.endswith('}')
    if len(tok)==1: return True
    if len(tok)==2 and tok[0]=='\\': return True
    return False

def ord_of(tok):
    if len(tok)==1: return ord(tok)
    if len(tok)==2 and tok[0]=='\\':
        esc=tok[1]
        if esc=='t': return ord('\t')
        if esc=='n': return ord('\n')
        if esc=='r': return ord('\r')
        return ord(esc)
    if tok.startswith(r'\u{'):
        try:
            return int(tok[tok.find('{')+1:tok.find('}')],16)
        except: return ord(tok[0])
    return ord(tok[0])

    if s.startswith(r'\u{') and s.count(r'\u{')==1 and s.endswith('}'): return s+'?'

        stripped=[b[len(pp):] for b in branches]

        non_empty=[s for s in stripped if s!=""]

            suffix=branches_to_regex(non_empty, cap, flags)

    has_empty=node.terminal

        else:

def eprint(*a, **kw):
    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, **kw)

def is_decimal(ch):
    return unicodedata.category(ch) == 'Nd'
def is_space(ch):
    return ch.isspace()
def is_word(ch):
    cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
    if cat.startswith('L'): return True
    if cat.startswith('M'): return True
    if cat == 'Nd': return True
    if cat == 'Pc': return True
    if ch == '_': return True
    return False

def escape_literal(ch):
    if ch == '\t': return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n': return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r': return r'\r'
    specials = set(r"\.^$|?*+()[]{}")
    if ch in specials:
        return '\\' + ch
    if ch == '-':
        return r'\-'
    return ch

def escape_class_char(ch):
    if ch == '\\': return r'\\'
    if ch == ']': return r'\]'
    if ch == '[': return r'\['
    if ch == '^': return r'\^'
    if ch == '-': return r'\-'
    if ch == '\t': return r'\t'
    if ch == '\n': return r'\n'
    if ch == '\r': return r'\r'
    return ch

def convert_char(ch, flags):
    if flags.get('digits') and is_decimal(ch):
        return r'\d'
    if flags.get('spaces') and is_space(ch):
        return r'\s'
    if flags.get('words') and is_word(ch):
        return r'\w'
    if flags.get('non_digits') and not is_decimal(ch):
        return r'\D'
    if flags.get('non_words') and not is_word(ch):
        return r'\W'
    if flags.get('non_spaces') and not is_space(ch):
        return r'\S'
    return None

def unicode_escape(ch, with_surrogates):
    code = ord(ch)
    if with_surrogates and code >= 0x10000:
        high = 0xD800 + ((code - 0x10000) >> 10)
        low = 0xDC00 + ((code - 0x10000) & 0x3FF)
        return f"\\u{{{high:x}}}\\u{{{low:x}}}"
    else:
        return f"\\u{{{code:x}}}"

def transform_string(s, flags):
    tokens=[]
    for ch in s:
        conv=convert_char(ch, flags)
        if conv is not None:
            tokens.append(conv)
            continue
        if flags.get('escape') and ord(ch) > 127:
            tokens.append(unicode_escape(ch, flags.get('with_surrogates', False)))
            continue
        tokens.append(escape_literal(ch))
    return tokens

class Node:
    def __init__(self):
        self.children={}
        self.terminal=False

def build_trie(lists):
    root=Node()
    for toks in lists:
        node=root
        for tok in toks:
            if tok not in node.children:
                node.children[tok]=Node()
            node=node.children[tok]
        node.terminal=True
    return root

def charset_for_tokens(toks):
    # toks are branch strings that are single char tokens
    orig=[]
    for tok in toks:
        if len(tok)==1:
            orig.append(tok)
        elif len(tok)==2 and tok[0]=='\\':
            esc=tok[1]
            if esc=='t': orig.append('\t')
            elif esc=='n': orig.append('\n')
            elif esc=='r': orig.append('\r')
            elif esc in '.^$|?*+()[]{}-\\': orig.append(esc)
            else: orig.append(esc)
        elif tok.startswith(r'\u{'):
            try:
                s=tok.find('{')+1
                e=tok.find('}')
                orig.append(chr(int(tok[s:e],16)))
            except:
                orig.append(tok)
        else:
            orig.append(tok)
    chars=sorted(orig, key=lambda c: ord(c))
    parts=[]
    i=0
    n=len(chars)
    while i < n:
        j=i
        while j+1<n and ord(chars[j+1])==ord(chars[j])+1:
            j+=1
        run=j-i+1
        if run>=3:
            parts.append(f"{escape_class_char(chars[i])}-{escape_class_char(chars[j])}")
        else:
            for k in range(i,j+1):
                parts.append(escape_class_char(chars[k]))
        i=j+1
    return f"[{''.join(parts)}]"

def lcp(lst):
    if not lst: return ""
    pref=lst[0]
    for s in lst[1:]:
        i=0
        lim=min(len(pref), len(s))
        while i<lim and pref[i]==s[i]:
            i+=1
        pref=pref[:i]
        if not pref: break
    return pref

def lcs(lst):
    if not lst: return ""
    rev=[s[::-1] for s in lst]
    rp=lcp(rev)
    return rp[::-1]

def is_single(tok):
    if tok in (r'\d',r'\D',r'\s',r'\S',r'\w',r'\W'): return False
    if tok.startswith('[') and tok.endswith(']'): return False
    if tok.startswith('('): return False
    if '{' in tok: return False
    if tok.startswith(r'\u{'):
        return tok.count(r'\u{')==1 and tok.endswith('}')
    if len(tok)==1: return True
    if len(tok)==2 and tok[0]=='\\': return True
    return False

def ord_of(tok):
    if len(tok)==1: return ord(tok)
    if len(tok)==2 and tok[0]=='\\':
        esc=tok[1]
        if esc=='t': return ord('\t')
        if esc=='n': return ord('\n')
        if esc=='r': return ord('\r')
        return ord(esc)
    if tok.startswith(r'\u{'):
        try:
            return int(tok[tok.find('{')+1:tok.find('}')],16)
        except: return ord(tok[0])
    return ord(tok[0])

def make_opt(s, cap):
    if not s: return ""
    if s.startswith('[') and s.endswith(']'): return s+'?'
    if s in (r'\d',r'\D',r'\s',r'\S',r'\w',r'\W',r'\t',r'\n',r'\r'): return s+'?'
    if len(s)==1: return s+'?'
    if len(s)==2 and s[0]=='\\': return s+'?'
    if s.startswith(r'\u{') and s.count(r'\u{')==1 and s.endswith('}'): return s+'?'
    pre='(' if cap else '(?:'
    return f"{pre}{s})?"

def branches_to_regex(branches, cap, flags):
    if not branches: return ""
    if len(branches)==1: return branches[0]
    if all(is_single(b) for b in branches):
        return charset_for_tokens(sorted(branches, key=ord_of))
    pp=lcp(branches)
    if pp:
        stripped=[b[len(pp):] for b in branches]
        has_empty="" in stripped
        non_empty=[s for s in stripped if s!=""]
        if not non_empty:
            return pp
        if has_empty:
            suffix=branches_to_regex(non_empty, cap, flags)
            return pp + make_opt(suffix, cap)
        else:
            suffix=branches_to_regex(non_empty, cap, flags)
            return pp + suffix
    ss=lcs(branches)
    if ss:
        stripped=[b[:-len(ss)] if ss else b for b in branches]
        has_empty="" in stripped
        non_empty=[s for s in stripped if s!=""]
        if not non_empty:
            return ss
        if has_empty:
            pre=branches_to_regex(non_empty, cap, flags)
            return make_opt(pre, cap) + ss
        else:
            pre=branches_to_regex(non_empty, cap, flags)
            return pre + ss
    singles=[b for b in branches if is_single(b)]
    multis=[b for b in branches if not is_single(b)]
    opts=[]
    if multis:
        opts.extend(sorted(multis))
    if singles:
        if len(singles)>=2:
            opts.append(charset_for_tokens(sorted(singles, key=ord_of)))
        else:
            opts.extend(singles)
    if len(opts)==1:
        return opts[0]
    pre='(' if cap else '(?:'
    return f"{pre}{'|'.join(opts)})"

def trie_to_regex(node, cap, flags):
    branches=[]
    for ch in sorted(node.children.keys()):
        child=node.children[ch]
        cr=trie_to_regex(child, cap, flags)
        branches.append(ch+cr)
    has_empty=node.terminal
    if not branches:
        return ""
    if has_empty:
        if len(branches)==1:
            return make_opt(branches[0], cap)
        else:
            alt=branches_to_regex(branches, cap, flags)
            return make_opt(alt, cap)
    else:
        if len(branches)==1:
            return branches[0]
        else:
            return branches_to_regex(branches, cap, flags)
